summary: The proof correctly derives a uniform compact gauge from John normalization, the accepted positive lower bound on D, the canonical tail bound, and the residual no-half-slice inequality. It then obtains simultaneous body, line, cell, midpoint-body, and global-triangle convergence, with the required area continuity and nondegeneracy. Continuity of the normalized Brunn--Minkowski cap deficit is established, and a zero-deficit closure point is correctly excluded: equality makes the positive-area limiting caps translates, the support argument extends the predecessor polygonal equality analysis to an arbitrary convex Hausdorff limit, and the resulting triangular-cap calculation forces D at least D_tr greater than 1/9, contradicting the inherited closure bound D at most 1/9. Scaling then gives the claimed universal positive modulus for arbitrary q.
